GridCN Design System and heca-grid-ui Specification
NIRI Scrollable-Tiling Layout Model
nodes.rationale: Horizontal scrolling columns with vertical workspaces; continuous scroll+snap for columns, discrete animated switch for workspaces. Two independent scrolling mechanisms on two axes.

nodes.label: ViewOffset Three-State Scroll Engine
nodes.rationale: Three states: Static(f64), Animation(spring/easing), Gesture(ViewGesture with velocity+snap). Core of NIRI's smooth horizontal scrolling. view_pos() = column_x(active_column) + view_offset.current().

nodes.label: Column Width No-Normalization Rule
nodes.rationale: Resize changes ONLY the active column's width. Other columns are NOT adjusted. No rebalancing. This is intentional — NIRI is a scrolling layout, not a fixed-grid tree. Columns overflow the viewport and you scroll to see the rest.

nodes.label: NIRI Overview/Expose Mode
nodes.rationale: Zoom out to see all workspaces as scaled-down thumbnails stacked vertically. Uses RescaleRenderElement + RelocateRenderElement. Triggered by 3-finger swipe down or keybind. Workspaces have Shadow elements for depth.

nodes.label: NIRI Workspace Switch Animation
nodes.rationale: Discrete index change between vertically arranged workspaces. Uses spring animation. Input goes to target workspace immediately (does not wait for animation to complete).

nodes.label: heca NIRI-Inspired Layout Engine
nodes.rationale: heca adopted NIRI's scrolling-column layout model after initially planning a BSP tree. Key insight: two-axis scrolling (continuous horizontal for columns, discrete vertical for workspaces) with ViewOffset managing horizontal scroll.

nodes.label: PaneBackend Content Abstraction Trait
nodes.rationale: Trait for all pane content sources: pane_type(), title(), set_size(), process_input(), update(), render_data(), should_close(). Implementations: TerminalBackend, NeovimBackend, FakeBackend, future BrowserBackend.

nodes.label: Tmux-Style Prefix Key Input Model
nodes.rationale: Deliberately tmux-style prefix (configurable, default Ctrl+B). NOT a bug to fix. Prevents conflicts with hosted terminal apps. 500ms prefix timeout. Double-press sends literal prefix to pane. Real modifier state passed (not hardcoded false).

nodes.label: Event-Driven Redraw Only
nodes.rationale: Chosen over continuous 60fps for efficiency. Only redraws when something changes. Uses needs_redraw flag. Prevents 100% GPU usage at idle.

nodes.label: Catppuccin Mocha Default Theme
nodes.rationale: Popular among developers, soft colors, good contrast. Bundled as fallback when no user theme exists.

nodes.label: Chrome Layout Architecture
nodes.rationale: Tab bar at top (32px), status bar at bottom (24px), left/right sidebars collapsible (200px expanded / 32px collapsed). All chrome rendered via wgpu primitives + cosmic-text in the same pass as pane content.

nodes.label: Floating as First-Class Space
nodes.rationale: Each workspace has two spaces: ScrollingSpace (tiling columns) and FloatingSpace (floating panes). toggle_float moves pane between them. Backend stays alive. NIRI approach corrected from initial ad-hoc float.

nodes.label: ActionRegistry Central Dispatch
nodes.rationale: HashMap<Discriminant<WmAction>, ActionHandler>. register() and execute() for all WM state changes. Registry bypasses are bugs. Parameterized variants share one handler via destructuring.

nodes.label: Interactive Move (Drag-to-Move Pane)
nodes.rationale: Three-phase drag: Starting (rubberband, pane stays in layout) → Moving (detached from layout, semi-transparent, follows pointer) → Drop (compute InsertPosition, animate into slot). Uses existing ViewOffset::Gesture for DnD edge scroll.

nodes.label: Focus Follows Mouse Behavior
nodes.rationale: On CursorMoved, if mouse over a different pane, focus switches. Configurable (default true). Debounce to avoid excessive switching when crossing gaps.

nodes.label: SGR Mouse Protocol Forwarding
nodes.rationale: SGR (1006) pure-ASCII mouse tracking protocol. Pixel coords converted to cell coords, sent as ESC[<button;col;rowM/m sequences to PTY. Depends on TerminalBackend being live (FakeBackend never enables mouse mode).

nodes.label: TerminalBackend (PTY + VTE)
nodes.rationale: First real pane content. Uses portable-pty for PTY spawning + alacritty_terminal for VTE parsing. Background reader thread feeds bytes into parser. Produces cell grid for rendering.

nodes.label: Neovim Grid Protocol Integration
nodes.rationale: msgpack-RPC client over stdio/socket. Parse ui_event redraw commands (grid_line, grid_cursor_goto, etc.). Must handle MULTIPLE grids (grid 1 = base, others = floating windows). Depends on terminal infrastructure (PTY spawning, reader threads, event-loop wakeup).

nodes.label: Session Persistence
nodes.rationale: Save workspace structure, column/pane layout, pane metadata (backend type, spawn command, CWD). Do NOT save PTY scrollback or nvim buffers. Restore: deserialize session, rebuild Session, respawn backends in saved CWDs.

nodes.label: heca-grid-ui GPU-Free Component Library
nodes.rationale: GPU-free component library. Emits Scene (DrawCommand display list); heca-renderer rasterizes. Signal-driven via floem_reactive facade. Taffy Flexbox for intra-component layout. Composition over inheritance: embed Base + impl Component.

nodes.label: Scene / DrawCommand Display List
nodes.rationale: GPU-free visual vocabulary. DrawCommand variants: Rect, Brackets, Text, Scanline, Gradient, PushClip/PopClip, Custom. Scene has two command lists: base commands and overlay commands (drawn after).

nodes.label: Overlay Layer for Popovers and Selects
nodes.rationale: Deferred overlay paint pass + overlay_active() routing. Scene gains overlay command list (always painted after base). Widgets report overlay_active() so event router gives them first dibs on pointer events. Needed by Select, Tooltip, Modal.

nodes.label: Reactive Signal System (floem_reactive facade)
nodes.rationale: Copy handle Signal<T>. .get() subscribes, .set() marks dirty. Memo/Effect for derived computations. Host coalesces dirty signals into repaint. Hidden behind heca_grid_ui::reactive facade (swappable).

nodes.label: Taffy Flexbox Layout for Intra-Component Arrangement
nodes.rationale: Taffy Flexbox/Grid/Block for widget layout inside panels. NOT a second WM layout engine — it never positions panes/columns. Strictly component-internal altitude.

nodes.label: Grid Theme/Intensity System
nodes.rationale: Token struct consumed by PaintCx. Presets: grid_tron() (cyan/dark default), grid_ares() (alternate). Intensity{Off, Low, Medium, Heavy} scales glow + scanlines globally. Tokens from global thread-local, set_grid_theme() updates all widgets next frame.

nodes.label: GridCN Tron/HUD Visual Design Language
nodes.rationale: TRON/neon HUD aesthetic: dark backgrounds, glowing cyan/red/orange borders, corner brackets, scanlines, monospace/HUD typography. 6 themes (tron, ares, clu, athena, aphrodite, poseidon). Progressive intensity from Off to Heavy.

nodes.label: winit Windowing Library
nodes.rationale: De-facto Rust windowing standard. Cross-platform (Linux/macOS/Windows). Handles HiDPI, monitor enumeration, raw keyboard scan codes. v0.30+ uses ApplicationHandler trait.

nodes.label: wgpu GPU API
nodes.rationale: Cross-platform GPU API (Vulkan/Metal/DX12/WebGPU). Safe Rust. Async. Used for all rendering including pane content and chrome compositing.

nodes.label: cosmic-text Text Rendering Library
nodes.rationale: Best pure-Rust text stack. Shaping, atlas caching, ligatures, variable fonts. Used by System76 Cosmic desktop. Provides FontSystem, SwashCache, Buffer for glyph rasterization.

nodes.label: alacritty_terminal VTE Library
nodes.rationale: Battle-tested VT parser available as Rust library crate. Feed PTY bytes, get cell grid.

nodes.label: portable-pty PTY Spawning Library
nodes.rationale: Cross-platform PTY creation. Works on Linux/macOS/Windows.

nodes.label: tokio Async Runtime
nodes.rationale: All IO flows through tokio: Neovim socket, PTY reader threads, RPC server.

nodes.label: rmpv MsgPack Library
nodes.rationale: Stable msgpack library used for Neovim msgpack-RPC protocol.

nodes.label: serde + toml for Config Parsing
nodes.rationale: serde for serialization/deserialization, toml for config file format. Used throughout heca for loading config.toml and theme files.

nodes.label: BSP Tree Layout (Original Plan, Later Replaced)
nodes.rationale: Phase 2 originally planned a binary BSP tree (i3-style). This was later replaced by NIRI scrolling columns after code analysis. BSP code in heca-core/src/pane.rs kept as deprecated reference.

nodes.label: Float/Unfloat Behavior Contract
nodes.rationale: prefix+f = float toggle. Originally tiled pane → unfloat restores original position. Spawned floating (no original slot) → unfloat places into new column. prefix+z reserved for column zoom (not float).

nodes.label: DnD Edge Auto-Scroll
nodes.rationale: When dragging near left/right viewport edges (<80px trigger zone), auto-scroll the layout. Uses normalized delta for scroll speed. Phase 3 should migrate from direct offset to ViewOffset::Gesture.

nodes.label: Sections Cannot Repeat Rule
nodes.source_location: exceptions: output/workspace by name, window-rule/layer-rule blocks

NIRI's 5 Core Design Principles
nodes.rationale: The five principles ensure predictable layout behavior: windows don't resize each other, focused windows stay stable, actions are immediate, disabled features have zero perf cost, and eye candy doesn't cause excessive rendering. These principles are the foundation of the scrollable tiling model.

nodes.label: Opening a New Window Does Not Affect Sizes of Existing Windows
nodes.rationale: Unlike BSP tiling where splits resize neighbors, scrollable tiling places new columns/panes alongside existing ones without reflow. This gives predictable layout behavior.

nodes.label: Focused Window Does Not Move on Its Own
nodes.rationale: Windows opening/closing/resizing left of the focused window should not visually move it. The view offset preserves the focused column's position.

nodes.label: Actions Should Apply Immediately
nodes.rationale: Input goes to the final target even during animations. State transitions are instant even if the visual catch-up animates. Prevents race conditions between input and layout state.

nodes.label: LazyClock — Consistent Time Queries per Iteration
heca Workspace Compositor — Single-Window GPU Host
Three-Layer Action Dispatch (Keyboard → Keymap → WmAction → Registry → Handler)
ActionRegistry — Central WM Action Dispatch
nodes.rationale: Replaces 500-line execute_action() match with registry-based dispatch. Every action gets a discriminant-keyed handler fn pointer, making the system traceable, hookable, and RPC-friendly.

nodes.label: KeymapRegistry — Mode-Specific Keybinding Lookup
nodes.rationale: Separates keybinding resolution from action handling. Per-mode maps (normal, global, sidebar) allow mode-specific keybindings without cluttering a single namespace.

nodes.label: Mixed WmAction Enum (Unit + Parameterized Variants)
nodes.rationale: Unit variants for keybindings (FocusLeft) and parameterized variants for RPC (Swap{a_id,b_id}). Both share one handler via discriminant dispatch.

nodes.label: RPC Command Parser — String to WmAction
SidebarTree — Workspace/Pane Tree Data Model
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the Session → Workspace → Column → Pane hierarchy with expand/collapse state and cursor tracking for keyboard navigation.

nodes.label: Collapsed Sidebar 40px Activity Strip
nodes.rationale: When sidebar is collapsed, shows workspace numbers + pane letters with activity bar indicators (solid for active, 50% for last visited, none for never visited). 40px width vs 32px previously.

nodes.label: Configurable Prefix Key Feature
nodes.rationale: Replaces hardcoded Ctrl+B with parsed KeyCombo from config. Users set prefix_key in config.toml for tmux/a-like or Alt/Space compatibility.

nodes.label: Global Non-Prefix Keybindings
nodes.rationale: Keys like Alt+1 or Super+b can trigger WM actions directly in Normal mode, before forwarding to terminal. Stolen from focused app, so users choose non-conflicting modifiers.

nodes.label: Chord Key Sequences (Multi-Key Prefix)
nodes.rationale: Extends prefix mode to accept multi-key chords (e.g., prefix+w+1 switches to workspace 1). Uses a trie-based ChordRegistry with timeout and Esc cancel.

nodes.label: Command Spawning from Keybindings
nodes.rationale: SpawnExternalCommand variant runs programs via portable-pty in new panes. Config: [[keys.command]] keys = prefix+g, command = lazygit.

nodes.label: heca Configuration System (TOML, Themes, Runtime Reload)
PaneBackend Trait — Content Source Abstraction
nodes.rationale: All content sources (terminal via alacritty_terminal, Neovim msgpack-RPC, future browser) implement the same trait. Allows plugging different backends without changing layout/rendering code.

nodes.label: Geist Mono Font (Embedded SIL OFL 1.1)
nodes.rationale: Default mono font for Grid UI. Embedded so look renders identically without system install. Theme.font_family/font_size remain configurable overrides.

hyperedges.label: Three-layer action dispatch system
hyperedges.rationale: Keyboard input flows through KeymapRegistry (key lookup) → WmAction (enum variant) → ActionRegistry (handler dispatch). InputMode controls which keymap is active. Together they form the complete WM action dispatch pipeline.

hyperedges.label: NIRI-inspired scrollable-tiling layout engine
hyperedges.rationale: Session manages Workspaces containing ScrollingSpace (horizontal columns) with animated ViewOffset. The entire layout model is inspired by NIRI's scrollable-tiling paradigm. Animation system drives smooth transitions for view scroll, workspace switch, and overview mode.

hyperedges.label: Pluggable chrome and container architecture vision
hyperedges.rationale: The future architecture separates sidebar shell from mounted containers. Pluggable chrome regions (left/right/top/bottom) host built-in and WASM-plugin containers. WorkspacesContainer is the first built-in container. WASM plugins contribute UI, register actions, and dispatch through the action system.

hyperedges.name: niri_scrolling_architecture
hyperedges.label: NIRI Two-Axis Scrolling Model
hyperedges.description: Horizontal columns scroll continuously with snap via ViewOffset; vertical workspaces switch discretely with animation. Two independent scrolling mechanisms for two axes.

hyperedges.name: heca_gpu_rendering_stack
hyperedges.label: heca GPU Rendering Stack
hyperedges.description: Core GPU stack: winit for windowing, wgpu for GPU API, cosmic-text for text rendering. All chrome and pane content composites in a single wgpu render pass. Event-driven redraw prevents wasted GPU cycles.

hyperedges.name: heca_grid_ui_architecture
hyperedges.label: heca-grid-ui Component Architecture
hyperedges.description: GPU-free component library producing Scene draw lists. Composable via embed-Base + impl-Component. Reactivity via signal system. Taffy for intra-component layout. Overlay layer for popovers. Themed via global Theme/Intensity tokens.

hyperedges.name: niri_animation_types
hyperedges.description: Three animation mechanisms in niri: physics-based spring, duration-based easing with curves, and GLSL fragment custom shaders for open/close/resize appearance

hyperedges.name: niri_layout_visual_chrome
hyperedges.description: Visual chrome and decoration elements configured in the layout section that render around and between windows: focus ring, border, shadow, tab indicator, insert hint, and struts

hyperedges.name: niri_window_sizing_modes
hyperedges.description: Four distinct window sizing modes: maximized column (full output width with gaps/borders), maximized-to-edges (no gaps/borders), fullscreen (entire screen with black backdrop), and windowed fullscreen (app thinks it's FS for screencasts). All remain in scrolling layout.

hyperedges.name: NIRI Scrollable Tiling Design
hyperedges.rationale: These five concepts together define NIRI's unique scrollable tiling layout model: windows coexist without reflow, focused windows stay stable, fractional scaling aligns to physical pixels, and workspaces auto-create/disappear. heca replicates this entire model.

hyperedges.name: heca Action Dispatch Pipeline
hyperedges.rationale: The complete chain from keyboard input through keymap resolution, WmAction variant construction (unit or parameterized), ActionRegistry dispatch by discriminant, and handler execution. Plans 01/02/03 all contribute to this pipeline.

hyperedges.name: NIRI Frame Scheduling System
hyperedges.rationale: The complete rendering pipeline from LazyClock (consistent per-iteration time) through AdjustableClock (slowdown factor) to RedrawState machine (Idle→Queued→WaitingForVBlank) and VBlank-synchronized frame submission.

hyperedges.name: Compositor Input Mode Architecture
hyperedges.shared_concept: The input mode system governing how keyboard input is interpreted in different compositor contexts (Normal, Prefix, PaneSelect, PaneSwap, SidebarNav, Rename, Chord, and user-defined Custom modes). Sticky vs non-sticky semantics control mode lifetime.

hyperedges.name: Keybinding Resolution Pipeline
hyperedges.shared_concept: End-to-end pipeline from key press to action dispatch: combo string syntax describes key sequences, KeyCombo struct represents parsed combos, binding precedence defines the check order (mode → prefix → global → terminal), and the prefix key mechanism gates prefix-mode bindings.

hyperedges.name: User Configuration Surface
hyperedges.shared_concept: User-facing configuration surface in config.toml covering unbinding defaults, spawning external commands, defining custom modes with triggers and bindings, and documented in both reference files.
